*The Regressive Backbone* is a statistics book with the working notes left in: at the bottom of every page you can see where the author is still weighing things up, and where he still has his doubts. [The first chapters](book/h0.html) are in English now; the rest, so far, only in [the Dutch edition](../manuscript/index.html){hreflang="nl"}. To practise as you read, three [exercise books in Dutch](../oefenboeken/broertjes/index.html){hreflang="nl"} go with it chapter by chapter, in R, JASP and SPSS; an English R one is planned.
:::

Exercise books in **SPSS, R and JASP** — most useful if you study at Leiden University, Hogeschool Leiden or Erasmus University, and for one-to-one help. Regression, ANOVA, psychometrics — step by step, with animals that behave badly. In Dutch for now; the first English ones are on their way.

A test statistic from a paper — *t*(38) = 2.24, *z* = 1.96 — and you see the *p*-value straight away, as an **area** under the curve, with the *z*, *t*, *F* and χ² tables beside it. A tool, not a toy — though it is in [the toy box](toys/index.qmd) too. ([in Dutch](../tabellen/index.html){hreflang="nl"})
:::

Four groups, one therapy, and a pretest that does something of its own. Step by step you take the first group's improvement apart into four pieces, until only one is left: what the pretest and the therapy do together. Then, as an encore, the same four pieces come out of a single regression. ([in Dutch](../speeltjes/solomon.html){hreflang="nl"})
:::

## The doubt is left in

<!-- MIEKE: "wat het boek over onzekerheid beweert, doet het ook zelf" — gekozen "it practises
     what it preaches about uncertainty" (Rosie's eigen woorden voor wat ze las); alternatief
     "it does what it says about uncertainty" (dichter bij het Nederlands, zonder preek).
     "met de stelligheid van iemand die nergens over heeft hoeven nadenken" — gekozen "the
     certainty of someone who has never had to think about anything" (Fable: dichter bij het
     Nederlands en droger); eerst "the confidence of someone who has never had to think
     anything over". -->
<!-- MIEKE (en_voorpagina, 25-10-2026): de opening staat weer hier, zoals in het Nederlands; tot
     vandaag stond ze als aanloop bovenaan (zie de BEN-notitie bij de held). Woordelijk de zin die
     daar stond, "Statistics is the one subject that takes uncertainty seriously; its textbooks
     rarely sound like it.", en daarna de bestaande tweede zin met "Most of them" in plaats van
     "Most statistics books" (anders twee keer "statistics" vlak na elkaar). "houdt die twee bij
     elkaar" blijft "doesn't" (Rosie: "the two what?"). -->
Statistics is the one subject that takes uncertainty seriously; its textbooks rarely sound like it. Most of them speak with the certainty of someone who has never had to think about anything. *The Regressive Backbone* doesn't: it practises what it preaches about uncertainty. Uncertainty is not a problem. It is contact with reality.

<!-- MIEKE: de knop heet in het (Nederlandse) boek "toon werknotities". Eerst stond dat label
     erbij; Rosie vroeg waarom haar een Nederlands woord werd verteld. Nu zonder label: "a button
     that opens the working notes". Of de Engelse hoofdstukken dezelfde knop krijgen, is nog niet
     besloten. "tweede leesniveau" — gekozen "a second way of reading"; alternatief "a second
     layer to read".
     Bijgewerkt 25-10-2026 (en_voorpagina): de Engelse hoofdstukken hebben de knop inmiddels —
     "✎ show working notes (n)", nagemeten in en/book/h0.html en h3.html. "every page of the book"
     klopt dus ook voor wie vanaf deze bladzij het Engelse boek opent. -->

That is why every page of the book ends with a button that opens the working notes. There are two kinds. The first is the workbench — wordings still to be chosen between, a figure still to come. The second is the doubt, and that one is about you: *does the reader see here that this is about the population, or does it need to be sharper?* Under a question like that, the extra explanation is right there. If you're following, you simply read on; if you stall, you open the note and find exactly that piece. It is not a peek behind the scenes. It is a second way of reading.

<!-- MIEKE: "Blijf jij op zo'n plek even haken" — gekozen "get stuck there for a moment";
     alternatief "snag on a place like that". "Je staat naast de auteur in plaats van onder
     hem" — de "hem" is de auteur, zoals in het Nederlands. -->
And it does something else. Where the material is hard, the page simply says so, in the words of someone who is still weighing up how to explain it. If you get stuck there for a moment, that is not down to you — that is where everyone's thinking stalls, the writer's included. You stand beside the author instead of beneath him. That's exactly where this book wants you to be.
